news.headline: 49ers without Bosa and Deebo Samuel; Mike Evans questionable
news.detail: As of Oct 19, San Francisco has Nick Bosa (knee/calf) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) out. WR Mike Evans (ribs) is questionable. Inactives come about 6:45 p.m. ET.

news.headline: Commanders lose RB Croskey-Merritt; Diggs questionable
news.detail: Washington ruled out its leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on Oct 17, plus backup QB Marcus Mariota. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable. Jayden Daniels has no game designation.

news.headline: Injuries on both sides; one outlet sees value on the Under
news.detail: Covers (Oct 19) says mounting injuries and a total of 52.5 could favor the Under. The list shows 51.5, so lines differ by book.

news.headline: Purdy's targets thinner with Samuel out, Evans doubtful-ish
news.detail: With Samuel out and Evans questionable, Kittle and Evans are expected to be Purdy's main targets. One outlet projects Purdy near 249 passing yards.

NFL.recap: The model's picks struggled in Week 6: it picked the winner in 5 of 12 games, was 3-9 against the spread and 4-8 on totals. Seven of its wrong winners came from games decided by efficiency or turnovers (ARI over LA, NO over NYG, CHI over ATL, CAR over PHI, CLE over BAL). It was wrong in all three games where it picked a different side than Vegas (NYG, ATL, PHI). Its average spread miss is 8.5 points against 6.9 for Vegas.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 3 graded games (NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR) where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 3 graded games with a gap of 4.9 points or more (CHI 6.6, CAR 5.2, BAL 4.9) won the over/under pick. Overall over/under is 4-8.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 5 of the 7 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as a main reason.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Big-game player picks hit less often than the model's chances say.
lessons.evidence: 1 of 8 big-game picks hit, against 2.8 expected. The milestone picks went 6 of 8, against 6.0 expected.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for 300+ yard and similar long-shot props, in buckets of model chance. Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are underperforming.
lessons.evidence: 1 of 5 best-value picks hit this season, against 2.7 expected, at -3.09 units.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

news.headline: Michigan State QB Milivojevic out at UCLA; freshman set to start
news.detail: ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Saturday that Alessio Milivojevic will miss the game. Backup Cam Fancher is also out, so true freshman Kayd Coffman, who has not thrown a college pass, is set to start. At least 11 Spartans are out, including the top four cornerbacks.

news.headline: UCLA is also on its backup QB
news.detail: UCLA's Nico Iamaleava is out for the season after knee surgery (reported Oct 19-20). Backup Ty Dieffenbach already has a 17-7 win over Wisconsin this year. Both teams are thin at quarterback, and Vegas has a low total of 42.5.

news.headline: UCF expected to start backup QB Jenkins against BYU
news.detail: ESPN reported on Oct 20 that Alonza Barnett III (hamstring) is not expected to start. He is listed questionable, and UCF's offensive coordinator said there is a fair chance he plays. Keyone Jenkins is set for a fifth straight start. UCF has 16 players on its injury report, and starting linebacker Lewis Carter is out.

news.headline: Eastern Michigan banged up, QB Noah Kim questionable
news.detail: Kim is questionable for the second straight week. A preview from Saturday also lists the offensive line and secondary as thin, plus receiver Nick Devereaux out. Ohio's QB Nick Poulos is back from a concussion and Ohio has won its MAC games so far.

news.headline: Troy QB Crowder questionable; WR TK Keyes out vs UL Monroe
news.detail: Troy QB Goose Crowder left last week's game twice with a shoulder injury and was called day-to-day. He was listed questionable this week. Receiver TK Keyes (13 catches, 282 yards) is out per the Sun Belt availability report. Troy lost 33-6 to Louisiana last week.

news.headline: Central Michigan QB Flores in concussion protocol
news.detail: Angel Flores, the run-heavy starter, was in concussion protocol as of Tuesday. An article from Saturday morning says his status was not likely to be known until near kickoff. Backup Jadyn Glasser would likely start. Miami (OH) is also on a backup QB, since starter David McComb and backup Thomas Gotkowski are out for the season. Caleb Heavner starts.

news.headline: Colorado thin at skill spots; Oklahoma State has a top offense
news.detail: Nine Buffaloes are on the injury report, including running back Micah Welch (possible fracture, no practice Tuesday). Two of QB Isaac Wilson's targets are out. Oklahoma State is described as the nation's fifth-best offense, led by QB Drew Mestemaker. Weak Colorado offense helps the under. A strong Oklahoma State offense pushes the other way.

news.headline: Boston College loses RB Dickens; Georgia Tech defense very thin
news.detail: Boston College running back Evan Dickens is out for the season, so QB Mason McKenzie, the team's top rusher, carries more of the load. Georgia Tech lists several defensive starters out (Noah Carter, Daiquan White, Savion Riley), and tackle Tawfiq Thomas is doubtful. Boston College is 2-10 on the road under its current coach.

College.recap: Week 8 results were mixed. The model picked the winner in 7 of 12 games, was 6-6 against the spread and 8-4 on over/under. Four of the five misses on winners were the model favoring a team more than Vegas did (NC State, Air Force, James Madison, Florida International); Duke over Virginia was the fifth. Those four favorites all lost outright and failed to cover. The three picks that ran against the market's favorite (Army, Marshall, Delaware's spread) did fine.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern may not hold up.
lessons.evidence: By my count in the Week 7-8 results listed, the over hit in 8 of 13 games where the model total was 3+ above Vegas (Week 7: 6 of 10; Week 8: 2 of 3). That is only slightly better than a coin flip, and the sample is under 20.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: Big misses mostly show up as efficiency gaps; turnovers and finishing drives come second.
lessons.evidence: In the 24 games missed by 8+ points in the earlier set, the top listed reason was efficiency in 17, turnovers in 4, finishing drives in 2 and defensive touchdowns in 1. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss. Week 8 results had no reviews, so no new data.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with the long-run average, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different favorite than Vegas, early results are mixed, not bad.
lessons.evidence: Now 6 games with a different favorite: the model was right in 3 (Missouri State, Army, Marshall) and wrong in 3 (Cincinnati, Old Dominion, Rice over Tulsa). The earlier 1-for-4 has evened out. Sample is tiny.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: When the model has the favorite winning by 3+ more points than Vegas, the favorite has mostly not covered.
lessons.evidence: In the Week 7-8 results listed, by my count 9 games fit (Utah, Fresno State, Houston, UCLA, NC State, Air Force, UConn, James Madison, Florida International). The favorite covered in 2 (UCLA over Wisconsin, UConn) and failed in 7. The earlier 6-for-6 count included games not in this list, and UCLA over Wisconsin contradicts a perfect record. Today's BYU (gap 8.4) and Troy (6.8) and Ohio (9.0) fit.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's favorite margin is 3+ points above Vegas's and check the cover rate by size of gap (3-6, 6+). Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak so far.
lessons.evidence: This season the list is 2 of 7 against 3.6 expected, at -3.18 units. Seven games is far too few to read, and the edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed).
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Need 20+ games per bucket.
